get.description:
Active categories in display order — backs the override picker and lets the UI
show a category's published range next to a race's measured distances.

schema.title: Response List Categories Api Categories Get

post.description:
Create a `Race` from selected `upload_ids` + segment assignment (§3 step
5). Every upload id is asserted to belong to the caller before anything is
created (§4 Tenancy); ambiguous sport detection is rejected with a clear
error naming the ambiguity rather than guessed at.

Attach further uploads to an existing race — backfilling a forgotten leg,
or replacing one recorded from the wrong device. `race_id` is resolved
through `get_owned_race` (404, not 403, for someone else's race); the
attached uploads go through the same ownership assertion as `/races/group`.

get.description:
Timeline list, newest first. Four bounded queries regardless of page
size: total count, the race page, official-result totals for that page,
and recorded totals for that page — never one query per race.

post.description:
A manually created race gets its conditions straight away when it is given a
location, since it has no import to enrich it and the date is already known.

get.description:
Full detail: race, official result, recorded activities (each with laps
and gear, no `gps_track`), fueling. Everything the detail page needs
except the GPS track (`/races/{id}/track`).

patch.description:
Metadata edit. Changing the **date or location re-runs weather enrichment**,
because those two fields are the entire input to the lookup — leaving the old
conditions attached would keep showing yesterday's weather for a corrected date,
which reads as data rather than as staleness. Any other edit leaves weather
alone.

The refetch cannot fail the edit: `enrich_weather` swallows every failure path
and simply leaves the existing values in place, so a slow or down archive costs
a moment, not the save. `POST /races/{id}/weather/refresh` remains available to
force a re-run without changing anything.

delete.description:
Cascades to official result, fuelings, recorded activities, their laps
and gear assignments — all declared `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` on
`Race`'s relationships.

post.description:
Re-run classification from the current primary recordings.

Always refreshes `auto_category`; only moves the assigned category when the user has
not overridden it. Useful after correcting a distance, switching which recording is
primary, or editing the category table itself.

put.description:
Full-replace semantics over the race's fueling rows, keyed by
`(race_id, segment)`: a segment present in the payload is upserted; a
segment that currently has a row but is **omitted** from the payload is
deleted. This is the natural reading of "upsert the whole set" for a form
that lets the user remove a segment's entry entirely (e.g. "actually I
didn't eat anything on the run") — a partial-merge semantic would have no
way to express a deletion at all.

schema.title: Response Upsert Fueling Api Races  Race Id  Fueling Put

get.description:
One polyline per segment, in race order. Only `is_primary` recordings —
the map shows the leg that counts, not every device that recorded it.
Derived transitions carry no track (§3 Grouping) and are skipped rather
than emitting an empty polyline. `?precision=full` returns the unsimplified
stream; anything else (including omission) goes through
`simplify_for_precision`.

Lap splits for the pacing chart, optionally filtered to one segment.
Only laps of `is_primary` activities. `sport` is denormalized onto
`LapSplit` precisely so this filter needs no extra join (§2 Indexes).

schema.title: Response Get Race Laps Api Races  Race Id  Laps Get

post.description:
Re-run weather enrichment for a race whose date or location was corrected
after import — and the way a manually entered race, which has no recording to
anchor to, gets its conditions at all.

`overwrite=True`: unlike import-time enrichment this is a deliberate re-run,
so it replaces whatever is there, including a previously-populated humidity.

Multipart upload of one or many files (§3 import flow). Each file is
handled independently — one bad or duplicate file in a batch never aborts
the others — and gets its own `UploadResult` with an explicit `outcome`
rather than a single pass/fail for the whole request.

`race_id`, if given, attaches every file directly to that existing race
instead of staging single-sport ones in the tray or auto-grouping a
multisport one into a new draft race.

schema.title: Response Create Uploads Api Uploads Post

get.description:
The ungrouped tray (§3 step 3), `?status=` filter, scoped to `user_id`
(§4 Tenancy — uploads are their own ownership root, never joined through a
race). Suggested groupings (§3 step 4) are always computed from every
*parsed* upload regardless of the filter, since a proposal only makes sense
over what's still ungrouped.

delete.description:
Discard an upload and its stored file.

Decision: an upload that is already `grouped` is **refused** (409), not
silently detached. Two reasons: (1) its stored file is the corpus §8
retention depends on for future re-imports as the parser improves — deleting
it out from under an active race's `RecordedActivity` rows would quietly
break that guarantee for exactly the uploads still in use; (2) detaching
would leave `RecordedActivity` rows with `upload_id=NULL` that look
unrecorded/orphaned in the UI despite representing real, still-valid data.
Removing a grouped upload's contribution to a race is a race-editing
operation (delete the race, or replace the recording via `attach`), not an
upload-tray operation.

patch.description:
Set `is_primary` and/or assign gear to this segment (§4, §5
`RecordingSwitch` + `GearPicker`).

get.description:
§2: retired gear is hidden from the default list (kept in history via
`?include_retired=true`); each item's distance is a live query, never a
stored counter.

schema.title: Response List Gear Api Gear Get

patch.description:
Edit or retire (`retired_at`) a gear item — retiring never touches past
`activity_gear` rows or the distance they contribute (§2).

get.description:
§3 step 3: sensor serials seen in this user's imports with no `GearDevice`
mapping yet.

schema.title: Response List Unknown Devices Api Gear Unknown Devices Get

post.description:
Maps a serial to `gear_id` and backfills every past activity (owned by
this user) that already recorded it (§3 step 3's payoff) — this is what lets
the user name a device once and have both past and future imports resolve
it.

CategoryKind.title: CategoryKind
CategoryKind.description:
What kind of category a `RaceCategory` row is.

The published DTU list mixes three things. Age classes (Schüler, Jugend, Junioren)
describe the *athlete*, and their distances overlap the open categories almost
entirely — Junioren is 0.75-1.5 / 20-40 / 5-10 against Kurzdistanz's 1.5 / 40 / 10 —
so a course cannot tell you which applies. Mixed Relay is a team format. Only
`DISTANCE` rows are eligible for automatic classification (§9).

ClassificationSource.title: ClassificationSource
ClassificationSource.description: Where a race's assigned category came from.

FuelingProduct.title: FuelingProduct
FuelingProduct.description:
One entry of `RaceFueling.products` — free-form, not a normalised catalogue
(§9 Open Decisions).

GearDeviceCreate.title: GearDeviceCreate
GearDeviceCreate.description:
`POST /gear/{id}/devices` — maps a serial to a gear item; backfills past
activities carrying that serial (§3 Gear detection).

GearDeviceMapped.title: GearDeviceMapped
GearDeviceMapped.description:
The `POST /gear/{id}/devices` response. Carries `backfilled_activity_count`
because the backfill *is* the payoff of naming a device (§3 Gear detection): the
user names a serial once and every past import carrying it resolves. Silently
updating history would leave them unable to tell whether it worked.

GearListItem.title: GearListItem
GearListItem.description:
`GET /gear` — inventory with accumulated distance per item (§2), computed
over `activity_gear` joined to primary `RecordedActivity` rows, plus
`distance_offset_m`. Not a stored column.

GearUpdate.title: GearUpdate
GearUpdate.description: `PATCH /gear/{id}` — edit or retire a gear item; all fields optional.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
`POST /auth/login` body. Deliberately not validated beyond shape — the
login endpoint gives the same error for a malformed/unknown email as for a
wrong password (§4), so there's nothing to gain from rejecting it earlier.

OfficialResultUpsert.title: OfficialResultUpsert
OfficialResultUpsert.description:
`PUT /races/{id}/official-result` body.

`total_time` is optional *here* but NOT NULL in the database: omit it and the server
sums the five splits. If any split is also missing there is nothing to sum, and the
request is refused with a message naming what to fill in — no zero, no guess.

RaceAttachRequest.title: RaceAttachRequest
RaceAttachRequest.description:
`POST /races/{id}/attach` body — attach further uploads to an existing
race, e.g. backfilling a leg or replacing one recorded from the wrong device.

RaceCategoryRead.title: RaceCategoryRead
RaceCategoryRead.description: A row of the distance-category table (§9).

RaceCreate.title: RaceCreate
RaceCreate.description:
`POST /races` — manual race creation.

No category: it is inferred from the measured distances once activities land (§9).
A race created by hand with no recordings stays unclassified until either an import
arrives or the user picks a category themselves.

RaceDetail.title: RaceDetail
RaceDetail.description:
`GET /races/{id}` — race + official result + recorded activities (each
with their laps and gear, no `gps_track`) + fueling. Everything the detail
page needs in one call except the GPS track (`/races/{id}/track`, its own
endpoint per §4 Payload note).

RaceFuelingUpsert.title: RaceFuelingUpsert
RaceFuelingUpsert.description: Full-replace request body: the complete set of fuelled segments for a race.

RaceFuelingUpsertItem.title: RaceFuelingUpsertItem
RaceFuelingUpsertItem.description: One row of the `PUT /races/{id}/fueling` request body.

RaceGroupRequest.title: RaceGroupRequest
RaceGroupRequest.description:
`POST /races/group` body: the upload ids the user selected plus, where
detection was ambiguous, an explicit segment assignment per upload id.

RaceListItem.title: RaceListItem
RaceListItem.description:
`GET /races` preview payload — deliberately excludes `gps_track`, lap
splits and raw activity rows; only what the timeline card needs (§4).

RaceListResponse.title: RaceListResponse
RaceListResponse.description:
`GET /races` envelope. Offset pagination over cursor: a race timeline is a
bounded, slow-growing per-user collection (dozens, not millions), so
offset's O(offset) cost is irrelevant, and `total` lets the UI render page
numbers without a second round trip.

RaceUpdate.title: RaceUpdate
RaceUpdate.description:
`PATCH /races/{id}` — metadata only (name, type, location, notes); every
field optional.

RecordedActivityDetail.title: RecordedActivityDetail
RecordedActivityDetail.description:
`RecordedActivityRead` plus the `GearPicker`'s last-used-shoes default
(§3: shoes can't be auto-detected, so the UI needs a suggestion to
pre-select) — `None` for any segment other than `run`, or once shoes are
already assigned.

RecordedActivityRead.title: RecordedActivityRead
RecordedActivityRead.description:
Mirrors `RecordedActivity` minus `gps_track` — this is the shape used in
`RaceDetail` and everywhere else except `/races/{id}/track` (§4 Payload note).

RecordedActivityUpdate.title: RecordedActivityUpdate
RecordedActivityUpdate.description:
`PATCH /activities/{id}` — set `is_primary`, or assign gear to this segment.
Gear assignment is a separate sub-object rather than a flat field because it
also carries `assigned_by`.

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description:
The five legs of a triathlon, in race order. Shared by `RaceFueling.segment`,
`RecordedActivity.segment` and `LapSplit.sport` (denormalized from its parent) —
one Postgres enum type (`segment`) backs all three columns.

SegmentSummary.title: SegmentSummary
SegmentSummary.description:
One segment's official-vs-recorded totals, as shown in the timeline
`SegmentBar` and the detail `SplitsComparison` table.

SegmentTrack.title: SegmentTrack
SegmentTrack.description:
One segment's polyline, as returned by `GET /races/{id}/track`. This is the
only place `gps_track` is ever serialised.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description:
Coarser sport classification used only for `Upload.detected_sport` — a
single-sport upload doesn't yet know whether it's a transition leg.

StatsSummary.title: StatsSummary
StatsSummary.description:
`GET /stats/summary` — the aggregate strip above the timeline. Computed
per-`user_id`, never an unscoped aggregate (§4 Tenancy).

TrackBoundsRead.title: TrackBoundsRead
TrackBoundsRead.description:
A segment's bounding box, for map viewport fitting without the frontend
having to scan `points` itself. Mirrors `RecordedActivity.bounds_*`.

UnknownDeviceRead.title: UnknownDeviceRead
UnknownDeviceRead.description:
`GET /gear/unknown-devices` — a sensor serial seen in imports with no gear
mapping yet (§3 Gear detection step 3).

UploadGroupProposal.title: UploadGroupProposal
UploadGroupProposal.description:
One suggested grouping surfaced by `GET /uploads?status=parsed` — a
proposal the user confirms, never auto-committed (§3 Single-sport uploads).

UploadRead.title: UploadRead
UploadRead.description:
Staging tray row. `stored_path` is a server-internal filesystem detail and
is deliberately not exposed, same spirit as omitting `password_hash` from
`UserRead`.

UploadResult.title: UploadResult
UploadResult.description:
One file's outcome from `POST /uploads` — the tray needs an explicit,
per-file status rather than a single batch-level response, because a
duplicate must be *reported*, not silently dropped (§3 "What Strava exports
actually look like": a user deliberately selecting three files can
legitimately get one distinct upload back, and the tray has to say so).

- ``created``   — parsed and stored as a new `Upload` (possibly auto-grouped
  into a race, if multisport, or attached to the `race_id` given in the
  request).
- ``duplicate`` — byte-identical to an upload this user already has;
  `upload` is the *existing* row, not a new one.
- ``failed``    — looked like a FIT file but failed to parse; still stored as
  an `Upload` row with `status=failed` so it's visible in the tray, not lost
  to a bare 400.
- ``rejected``  — rejected before parsing was even attempted (oversized, or
  not a `.fit` file per its name) — no `Upload` row is created for this case,
  since nothing was actually staged.

UploadTrayResponse.title: UploadTrayResponse
UploadTrayResponse.description:
`GET /uploads` response — the ungrouped tray plus suggested groupings.
Proposals are always computed over every *parsed* (ungrouped) upload
regardless of the `?status=` filter applied to `uploads`, since a proposal
only makes sense over what's still sitting in the tray.

UserRead.title: UserRead
UserRead.description:
`GET /auth/me` and any embedded owner reference. Never includes
`password_hash`.
